title: Execution of the ceiling cube-root program
statement: Let $P$ be a finite program, let $p,n,d$ be natural numbers, let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$, and let the limits have word bound $W$. Suppose the program at position $p$ is the specified loop program that starts a candidate at $0$, increments it while its cube is less than the input, and then writes the candidate to the argument location. If $8n+1\le W$, then this program call, with input list $[n]$, memory $\mu$, and depth parameter $d$, finishes within $12r+12$ steps, where $r$ is the least natural number satisfying $n\le r^3$; it returns $r$ in location $0$ and leaves memory equal to $\mu$.
hypotheses_covered: $P[p]$ is the specified ceiling cube-root program
$\mu$ is a memory function from natural numbers to integers
$8n+1$ is at most the word bound
